summary: Durnesswick final client report DL_2020_0050 (September 28, 2020) for Nimbravelle Medicines Inc: NM-12 oral vehicle follow-up. The cosolvent vehicle (PEG400/water 30:70) dissolved NM-12 at 10 mg/mL but precipitated on dilution into simulated gastric fluid and was rejected. A dispersed suspension in 0.5% methylcellulose is recommended provisionally, with a recipe card, preparation sequence, homogeneity check and the limits of the evidence.
header: DL_2020_0050 | Nimbravelle Medicines Inc | Final Report R1

title_block.title: NM-12 Oral Vehicle: Precipitation-on-Dilution Follow-up
title_block.subtitle: Final Report
lines: Prepared by: Dr J. Carver, Formulation Development Lead

blocks.p: Nimbravelle needed a 10 mg/mL oral vehicle for NM-12 for repeat-dose rodent studies. The cosolvent vehicle selected earlier (PEG400/water 30:70) gave a clear solution at 10 mg/mL but precipitated within minutes when diluted into simulated gastric fluid. We recommend, provisionally, a dispersed suspension in 0.5% methylcellulose, which was easily redispersed after 24 hours. Chemical stability and dose homogeneity over the dosing period must be confirmed before the first study.

list: NM-12 drug substance, lot NM12-DS-04 (client CoA), micronised
Excipients: methylcellulose (400 cP grade), hydroxypropyl methylcellulose, polysorbate 80, PEG400, hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin, all compendial grade
Simulated gastric fluid without pepsin (SGF), pH 1.2, prepared fresh

blocks.p: Eight vehicles were screened. Equilibrium solubility was measured by shake-flask; appearance and 24-hour physical stability were assessed on separately prepared 10 mg/mL formulations. This is an exploratory screen, not a locked process.

Each 10 mg/mL formulation was diluted 1:10 into SGF at 37 °C with gentle stirring and observed for 30 minutes against a black and a white background. Vehicle-only dilutions were run alongside as controls.

rows: Turbid within 2 min; crystalline precipitate by 10 min
Fine haze at 5 min, settling by 30 min
Particles dispersed; no visible change in particle appearance
table.caption: Table 2 Dilution observations

blocks.p: The cosolvent vehicles precipitated on dilution, so the earlier solution approach is rejected.

list: Disperse methylcellulose in one third of the water at 80 °C, then add the remaining water cold and stir until clear
Wet the NM-12 powder with a small volume of vehicle to a paste, then add the rest in portions with stirring
Stir continuously during dosing; dose volume 10 mL/kg
Before the first dose, sample top, middle and bottom and confirm homogeneity by HPLC
Chemical stability of NM-12 in the vehicle beyond the day of preparation was not tested; until it is, prepare fresh daily
Dose homogeneity and redispersibility were assessed visually only
Particle size was not controlled; if exposure is variable in the first study, a milled suspension should be evaluated
